subject: JAM
name: Jamaica
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. claims.title: Taino settlement of Xaymaca
claims.summary: Arawak-speaking peoples settle the island they call Xaymaca, building villages led by caciques and farming cassava and corn.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-600-taino-settlement-of-xaymaca, claim TL:JAM:event:600:taino-settlement-of-xaymaca, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Columbus reaches Jamaica
claims.summary: On his second voyage Christopher Columbus arrives off the north coast, claiming the island for Spain and naming a harbour Santa Gloria.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1494-columbus-reaches-jamaica, claim TL:JAM:event:1494:columbus-reaches-jamaica, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sevilla la Nueva founded
claims.summary: Spain establishes its first permanent settlement on the north coast, beginning a colonial era that all but exterminates the Taino.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1509-sevilla-la-nueva-founded, claim TL:JAM:event:1509:sevilla-la-nueva-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: English conquest
claims.summary: An English force under Penn and Venables seizes the island for Cromwell, launching the sugar-and-slavery plantation economy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1655-english-conquest, claim TL:JAM:event:1655:english-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Port Royal earthquake
claims.summary: A powerful earthquake and tsunami sink much of the buccaneer city of Port Royal, killing thousands and ending its golden age.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1692-port-royal-earthquake, claim TL:JAM:event:1692:port-royal-earthquake, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Maroon treaties
claims.summary: Treaties with Cudjoe's Leeward Maroons and Nanny's Windward Maroons end the First Maroon War, granting them land and autonomy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1739-maroon-treaties, claim TL:JAM:event:1739:maroon-treaties, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tacky's Revolt
claims.summary: A major slave rebellion led by the Akan leader Tacky sweeps the island before being crushed with the aid of the Maroons.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1760-tacky-s-revolt, claim TL:JAM:event:1760:tacky-s-revolt, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Baptist War
claims.summary: Samuel Sharpe leads a Christmas rebellion of tens of thousands; its suppression hastens the end of slavery in the empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1831-the-baptist-war, claim TL:JAM:event:1831:the-baptist-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Emancipation
claims.summary: After the Abolition Act of 1833 and a period of apprenticeship, the enslaved people of Jamaica gain full freedom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1838-emancipation, claim TL:JAM:event:1838:emancipation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Morant Bay rebellion
claims.summary: Paul Bogle's uprising is brutally crushed; Bogle and George William Gordon are executed, and Jamaica becomes a crown colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1865-morant-bay-rebellion, claim TL:JAM:event:1865:morant-bay-rebellion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Garvey founds the UNIA
claims.summary: Marcus Garvey establishes the Universal Negro Improvement Association, building the largest Pan-African movement of its age.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1914-garvey-founds-the-unia, claim TL:JAM:event:1914:garvey-founds-the-unia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Birth of Rastafari
claims.summary: The Rastafari movement emerges in Jamaica after the crowning of Haile Selassie I, drawing on Garvey's vision of African redemption.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1930-birth-of-rastafari, claim TL:JAM:event:1930:birth-of-rastafari, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Labour rebellions
claims.summary: Island-wide worker uprisings give rise to Bustamante's union and Manley's PNP, founding modern Jamaican party politics.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1938-labour-rebellions, claim TL:JAM:event:1938:labour-rebellions, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Universal adult suffrage
claims.summary: A new constitution grants every adult the vote, the first in the British Caribbean, and Jamaica holds its first elections under it.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1944-universal-adult-suffrage, claim TL:JAM:event:1944:universal-adult-suffrage, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: West Indies Federation
claims.summary: Jamaica joins the federation of British Caribbean colonies as its largest member, an experiment in regional union.

sources.label: The Federal Archives Fonds, 1958-1962 (West Indies Federation)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1958-west-indies-federation, claim TL:JAM:event:1958:west-indies-federation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Referendum to leave the federation
claims.summary: Jamaicans vote to withdraw from the West Indies Federation, dooming it and opening the way to separate independence.

sources.label: The Federal Archives Fonds, 1958-1962 (West Indies Federation)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1961-referendum-to-leave-the-federation, claim TL:JAM:event:1961:referendum-to-leave-the-federation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence
claims.summary: Jamaica becomes an independent nation within the Commonwealth, with Alexander Bustamante as its first prime minister.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1962-independence, claim TL:JAM:event:1962:independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Two-party democracy
claims.summary: Independent Jamaica settles into a competitive democracy contested by the JLP and the PNP, with peaceful alternations of power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1962-two-party-democracy, claim TL:JAM:event:1962:two-party-democracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reggae goes global
claims.summary: Bob Marley and the Wailers bring reggae and the Rastafari message to a worldwide audience, making Jamaica a cultural superpower.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-1973-reggae-goes-global, claim TL:JAM:event:1973:reggae-goes-global, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bolt's sprinting dynasty
claims.summary: Usain Bolt wins the 100m and 200m at three straight Olympics, cementing Jamaica's dominance of world sprinting.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-2008-bolt-s-sprinting-dynasty, claim TL:JAM:event:2008:bolt-s-sprinting-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: World Heritage inscription
claims.summary: The Blue and John Crow Mountains, refuge of the Maroons, become Jamaica's first UNESCO World Heritage Site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jamaica: From the Taino land of Xaymaca to a sovereign Caribbean nation whose reggae and runners carry its name across the world.", terralore.co/country/JAM/chronicle#ev-2015-world-heritage-inscription, claim TL:JAM:event:2015:world-heritage-inscription, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
